SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which school transport is safe? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger's car
   B. An overloaded vehicle
   C. A vehicle with no seats
   D. A vehicle approved by school and parents

2. Which of these is a child right? (1 mark)
   A. To be married early
   B. To work in a quarry
   C. To be beaten
   D. To go to school

3. Whose fault is it if a child is abused? (1 mark)
   A. The child
   B. The abuser, never the child
   C. The teacher only
   D. The neighbour

4. Which of these is a benefit of democracy in school? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone has a voice
   B. Leaders are never checked
   C. Only some pupils are heard
   D. Pupils are ignored

5. Which shows respect for the minority? (1 mark)
   A. Listening to those who did not win
   B. Sending them away
   C. Ignoring them
   D. Laughing at them

6. What does majority mean? (1 mark)
   A. A tie
   B. The larger number of votes
   C. No votes
   D. The smaller number of votes

7. Which shows respect for the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring leaders
   B. Insulting leaders
   C. Following fair instructions politely
   D. Laughing at them

8. Which minister would deal with dirty toilets? (1 mark)
   A. Music
   B. Sports
   C. Library
   D. Health and sanitation

9. What is a Children's Government in school? (1 mark)
   A. The government of Kenya
   B. A group of parents
   C. A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   D. A group of teachers

10. Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting? (1 mark)
   A. The patron
   B. The Speaker
   C. The secretary
   D. The president

11. Which quality is important for a pupil leader? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Laziness
   C. Honesty
   D. Selfishness

12. In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening? (1 mark)
   A. Fight
   B. Leave
   C. Close the meeting
   D. Read the last minutes

13. Which of these leads prayers in a mosque? (1 mark)
   A. A tailor
   B. A cook
   C. An imam
   D. A nurse

14. Who is a good resource person to learn about community leadership? (1 mark)
   A. A cartoon
   B. A random shop
   C. A village elder
   D. A stranger who knows nothing

15. Which of these is a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. A farmer
   B. A trader
   C. A driver
   D. A pastor

16. What do clan elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Repair roads
   B. Sell tickets
   C. Cook school lunch
   D. Keep customs and settle disputes

17. Who is the head of the national government? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The MCA
   C. The Governor
   D. The President

18. Who leads the meetings of the county assembly? (1 mark)
   A. The chief
   B. The driver
   C. The Speaker
   D. The governor

19. Which of these tasks belongs to the county government? (1 mark)
   A. Immigration
   B. National defence
   C. County roads
   D. Foreign affairs

20. Who approves the governor's choice of county executive committee members? (1 mark)
   A. The county assembly
   B. The chief
   C. The village elder
   D. The teachers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three benefits of democracy in school. (3 marks)

22. In a class election, Maria got 14 votes, Juma got 9 votes and 2 papers were spoilt. How many pupils voted? Who won? Show working. (3 marks)

23. Describe how an ordinary pupil can support the Children's Government. (3 marks)

24. Name four members of a typical Children's Government. (4 marks)

25. Give four services provided by county governments. (4 marks)

26. Explain why a Children's Government should not punish pupils. (3 marks)

27. Name three kinds of community leaders. (3 marks)

28. Explain why early marriage is against the rights of a child. (5 marks)

29. What is a county assembly? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A vehicle approved by school and parents
   Approved vehicles are safer.

2. D — To go to school
   Children have the right to education.

3. B — The abuser, never the child
   Abuse is never the child's fault.

4. A — Everyone has a voice
   Democracy makes everyone heard.

5. A — Listening to those who did not win
   Democracy includes everyone.

6. B — The larger number of votes
   Majority means more than others.

7. C — Following fair instructions politely
   Respect includes obeying fair instructions.

8. D — Health and sanitation
   Health and sanitation looks after cleanliness.

9. C — A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   It is made up of pupils chosen by their classmates.

10. C — The secretary
   The secretary keeps the minutes.

11. C — Honesty
   Leaders must be honest and fair.

12. D — Read the last minutes
   Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

13. C — An imam
   An imam leads prayers.

14. C — A village elder
   A village elder knows leadership.

15. D — A pastor
   Pastors lead worship.

16. D — Keep customs and settle disputes
   Clan elders guard customs and settle quarrels.

17. D — The President
   The President leads the national government.

18. C — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads the assembly.

19. C — County roads
   County roads belong to the county.

20. A — The county assembly
   The assembly must approve them.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone has a voice, decisions are fair, and pupils obey rules they helped to make.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 25 pupils voted. Maria won.
   Working / marking points: 14 + 9 + 2 = 25. 14 is more than 9, so Maria won. 1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the winner, 1 mark for showing working.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Vote for leaders, follow fair instructions, and give ideas through the class representative.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: President, deputy president, Speaker, and class representatives. Accept cabinet members or secretary.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each member.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each service.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Only teachers decide on discipline, pupil leaders may be unfair, and serious problems must be reported to teachers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Religious leaders, clan elders and village elders. Accept chiefs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each kind.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: It stops a child from going to school. It harms health. It takes away childhood and play. It is against the law because the age of marriage is 18. It limits the child's future.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.
